title: E8 self-duality does not supply a forced inverse for an arbitrary map
description: Self-duality L_E8* isomorphic to L_E8 is established. It does not imply that every linear map Phi into E8 has a coordinate-free inverse Psi = Phi* with Psi o Phi = id. The Moore-Penrose inverse B = (A^T A)^{-1} A^T exists for full column rank and is independent of the lattice being unimodular. The extra claim ||Phi(v)|| = (h/c^2) f(v) is not forced by m = hf/c^2.
stop_reason: A*A = I holds only if A is already an isometry on the chosen subset. Self-duality of E8 does not select A. Close this STOP only with an explicit Weyl element or lattice automorphism that inverts the named map without a rank or subset choice.
definitions: E8 self-duality: the even unimodular lattice equals its dual.
Forced inverse: Psi o Phi = id on a named domain with no extra rank or coordinate choice.
Moore-Penrose inverse: the least-squares inverse of a full-column-rank matrix.
equations: A* A = I only if A is an isometry on the named subset
assumptions: E8 is the unique even unimodular lattice in dimension 8.
m = hf/c^2 converts a named energy quantum, not an arbitrary embedding into R^8.
mechanism: Keep the lattice EST. Park the loop claim until the map is a named automorphism, not a pseudoinverse dressed as duality.
falsification_conditions: A named A in W(E8) or Aut(L_E8) with A^{-1} = A* on a predeclared domain.
A derivation that m = hf/c^2 selects that A uniquely.
confusion_guard: Self-dual lattice is not the same as invertible embedding. Do not treat a generated loop diagram as a proof.
primary_sources: Conway & Sloane, Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups
Bourbaki, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Ch. VI
predictions: Any even unimodular lattice in dimension 8 remains isometric to E8.
Pseudoinverse loops will keep requiring a rank hypothesis.
